nodes.label: Refresh Rotation with Family Reuse Detection
nodes.rationale: Every refresh issues a new token and invalidates the old one. If a spent token is presented again, revoke the whole family and force re-authentication — a legitimate client never replays one, so this turns a silent compromise into a detected one.
nodes.norm_label: refresh rotation with family reuse detection

nodes.label: Q5 — Staff MFA Gap
nodes.rationale: The one place where the build plan's closed six-endpoint auth list and the security document's 'without exception' requirement pointed in different directions: inventing an MFA flow would violate rule 2 to satisfy rule 3. Flagged rather than silently resolved, then closed in Stage 19 with TOTP, encrypted secrets, recovery codes and a separate challenge JWT audience.

nodes.label: Stage 19 — Staff MFA
nodes.rationale: TOTP via otplib rather than an SMS second factor, which would depend on Stage 18's provider and is the weakest common second factor. Enrollment shows an otpauth:// QR, which reuses Stage 16's renderer — so Stage 16 must come first. Enrollment is forced on first login because 'without exception' means the un-enrolled state cannot reach anything.

nodes.label: npm run mfa:code Development Helper
nodes.rationale: Reads the account's stored secret, decrypts it and prints a fresh code every 30 seconds. Deliberately not an echo inside the sign-in path — a TOTP code is a function of the clock, so a code printed at sign-in would expire while you read it and the replay check would refuse the retry. Exits unless NODE_ENV=development, and being a script nobody invokes it cannot be left switched on the way a flag can.

nodes.label: MFA on Dashboard Accounts — Confirmed
nodes.rationale: The challenge is signed for a separate JWT audience so the existing audience check rejects it anywhere an access token is expected — separation enforced by a control that already existed rather than a new rule someone has to remember. A TOTP code cannot be replayed, verification is rate-limited per account rather than per IP, and the account is re-read at every step so instant revocation holds inside the window between password and second factor.

nodes.label: No MFA Reset Path and No Step-Up Re-Authentication
nodes.rationale: An account that loses both its authenticator and its recovery codes is locked out permanently. A reset is itself security-sensitive — whoever can reset MFA can take over an administrator account — so it needs dual control or an out-of-band identity check rather than a convenient endpoint. Export and benefit editing sit behind permissions and the audit log but not behind a fresh second factor.
nodes.norm_label: no mfa reset path and no step-up re-authentication

nodes.label: Consent Records a Declined Channel Explicitly
nodes.rationale: Writing nothing for a refusal makes 'declined' and 'never asked' indistinguishable a year later, which is exactly the question a complaint would raise. Both channels are required in the claim payload so an omission is never silently read as consent.
nodes.norm_label: consent records a declined channel explicitly

nodes.label: MFA Scope Resolved from the Narrower Sentence
nodes.rationale: The security document says both 'mandatory on every dashboard account, without exception' and 'MFA for any staff account that can reach more than the verification page'. The second is the specific statement and resolves the first. TOTP via otplib, secret encrypted with AES-256-GCM, ten Argon2id-hashed single-use recovery codes.
nodes.norm_label: mfa scope resolved from the narrower sentence

nodes.label: Refresh Tokens Hashed with SHA-256
nodes.rationale: A refresh token is 256 bits of server-generated randomness, not a low-entropy human secret. Argon2id's deliberate slowness defends nothing and adds per-request latency; the only property needed is unlinkability from a DB leak, which SHA-256 provides.

nodes.label: Dashboard Refreshes Through One Shared Promise
nodes.rationale: The admin landing screen opens with five requests at once, so ten minutes after sign-in all five 401'd together and rotated the same cookie in parallel: the first won, the other four read as replay, and the family died. A twelve-hour refresh token destroyed by a ten-minute access token. The server was left alone deliberately — widening rotation would weaken theft detection to compensate for a client defect.
nodes.norm_label: dashboard refreshes through one shared promise

nodes.label: STAFF_MFA_REQUIRED Development Switch
nodes.rationale: Defaults to true; anything but the exact string 'false' is true so a typo fails closed; and loadEnv refuses to return if it is false while NODE_ENV=production — a boot failure rather than a warning. Nothing is deleted when it is off. A password-only sign-in audits as auth.mfa.skipped, never auth.login.success, because a trail that recorded them identically would hide the only rows that could evidence a misconfiguration.

nodes.label: TOTP Replay Guard Looks Like Flakiness
nodes.rationale: StaffUser.mfaLastUsedEpoch refuses a code at or before the last used period even when cryptographically valid, which is what stops one observed over a shoulder being replayed. It surfaces as acceptance-journey.test.ts failing 401 at step 1 when the seeded administrator signs in twice inside the same 30-second window — precisely what you do when investigating a failure. Wait half a minute; do not weaken the replay check.
nodes.norm_label: totp replay guard looks like flakiness

nodes.label: STAFF_MFA_REQUIRED Caveat on the MFA Claim
nodes.rationale: Named here rather than only in the decision log, because the heading claims enforcement on every dashboard account and that claim now carries a condition. What makes it acceptable is that it cannot be turned in the place where turning it matters — loadEnv throws in production, the handler re-checks at the branch, a typo fails closed, and the resulting sign-in audits distinctly.
nodes.norm_label: staff_mfa_required caveat on the mfa claim

nodes.label: API Hardening
nodes.rationale: Schema validation at the edge rejecting unknown fields rather than ignoring them, since mass-assignment flaws come from silently accepting extra keys. Parameterised queries only. Rate limiting by class, per IP and per principal. Exact-origin CORS allowlist, never a wildcard and never reflecting Origin. HSTS with preload, nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, strict CSP without unsafe-inline. Certificate pinning in the member app. Pagination caps.

nodes.label: Client Token Storage Rules
nodes.rationale: httpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict refresh cookie for the panel and never localStorage, because any XSS flaw becomes total account theft. The access token stays in memory and state-changing routes use its bearer header. Keychain/Keystore on native. No tokens in URLs — they reach logs, history and referrer headers.

nodes.label: Stage Ledger 0 to 28
nodes.rationale: Stages 0-14 built the logic under the build plan; 15-24 are defined in the roadmap; 25-28 were added later. Complete: 0-14, 16-19, 25-28. Remaining: 20 (hardening), 21 (deployment), 22 (Arabic/RTL), 24 (pre-launch); 15 and 23 are partial.

nodes.label: Stage 20 — Hardening for a Public Network
nodes.rationale: The five deferred security-review items: security headers and CORS, httpOnly cookies and CSRF, secret management, edge rate limiting, and alerting. Everything built so far assumed localhost. Give the JWT secret a kid now, even with one key, so rotation later does not need a flag day.
nodes.norm_label: stage 20 — hardening for a public network

nodes.label: Checklist Status Summary
nodes.rationale: 23 confirmed, 3 partial, 4 deferred of 30. Deferred items are listed with the same prominence as confirmed ones because a review that buries them is worth nothing. None are oversights: each is an integration no reference document specifies, or deployment-shaped work Stage 21 settles.

nodes.label: Deferred — Real-Time Alerting
nodes.rationale: Every alertable event — repeated failed lookups, refresh-token reuse, bulk export, out-of-hours access, excess lookup volume, denial spikes — is recorded with a distinct audit action, so the data exists. Nothing consumes it, and no alerting destination is named in any reference document. This is what makes the audit log forensic rather than preventive.

nodes.label: Deferred — httpOnly Cookies and CSRF
nodes.rationale: Mitigated at review time by no client storing a token in localStorage or sessionStorage — all held it in a module-scoped variable, unreadable by an injected script and gone when the tab closes, at the cost of a sign-in on every reload. Residual risk: bearer tokens in JavaScript memory remain reachable by XSS in the same context. Later addressed by the httpOnly refresh cookie decision.

nodes.label: Deferred — Security Headers and CORS Allowlist
nodes.rationale: The item most likely to be forgotten, because everything works without it right up until it is deployed. In development the clients reach the API through a Vite proxy, so requests are same-origin and no CORS policy is exercised — the gap is invisible locally and appears immediately on first deployment. CORS_ORIGIN_* variables are named in .env.example but unread.
nodes.norm_label: deferred — security headers and cors allowlist

nodes.label: Deferred — Pepper and Signing Keys in a KMS
nodes.rationale: No KMS exists in this build's stack or in any reference document. PASSWORD_PEPPER is an environment variable — at least not colocated with the hashes it protects, which is the property the pepper exists for, but not the mechanism required. The same applies to the verification-session HMAC secret and the JWT signing key, and to key rotation with a kid so old tokens verify during rollover.
nodes.norm_label: deferred — pepper and signing keys in a kms

nodes.label: What I Would Fix First
nodes.rationale: In order: MFA on dashboard accounts, security headers and a CORS allowlist, httpOnly cookies with CSRF, alerting, then a KMS retiring three environment-variable secrets. Items 2 and 3 are ordinary deployment work; item 1 was a conflict between the build plan and the security specification needing a human to resolve it.

nodes.label: Partial Items: Anonymisation, Special-Category Data, Pagination Caps
nodes.rationale: No anonymisation endpoint exists and no stage lists one. No special-category data is satisfied by construction — Redemption has no treatment column — but marked partial because the guard is the schema as it stands, not a test. The export cap of 5000 rows is high enough that the full membership is effectively reachable, so the cap is not doing protective work there.
nodes.norm_label: partial items: anonymisation, special-category data, pagination caps

nodes.label: Refresh Token Moves to an httpOnly Cookie
nodes.rationale: A module-scoped variable cost a sign-in on every page reload. The cookie is held by the browser rather than the page, so it survives a reload and document.cookie cannot see it. No CSRF token because SameSite=Strict, Path=/auth/refresh and an unreadable cross-origin response close the gap together — a CSRF token becomes necessary the moment any state-changing route authenticates by cookie.
nodes.norm_label: refresh token moves to an httponly cookie

nodes.label: IDENTITY_CODE_HMAC_SECRET Rotation
nodes.rationale: Rotating it invalidates every printed card at once — which is also the only recovery a printed credential has. So the value must be in the secret manager and backed up before a print run, not generated casually at deploy time.

nodes.label: QR Well
nodes.source_location: fill="#ffffff" rounded region on the reverse
nodes.rationale: A rounded white panel drawn into the back artwork itself, reserved for the membership QR symbol. Because the artwork is loaded through it cannot receive per-member content, so the live code is laid over this well as a second SVG layer — both layers stay vector, so the card is sharp at every size. The well is padded by 4/45 on each side to reserve the four-module quiet zone scanners need around the 37 live modules of a level-M code.

nodes.label: Charcoal Card Gradient
nodes.rationale: The card's ground: a 48-stop linear ramp from #221C1B to #4A4240 running along (0.077, 0.053) to (306.696, 486.629) over a 540x340 face — about 147.8deg in CSS terms — and holding the darkest value flat for roughly the first tenth before it opens up. Both faces of the card declare the identical ramp; the back re-expresses the same values as rgb percentages under a 0.749 gradientTransform. It shows through at the transparent corners and in the moment before the artwork loads, so the CSS variable that stands in for it is derived from these exact numbers rather than approximated — a 135deg guess reads as a visible seam against the artwork.

nodes.label: Steigenberger Wordmark Stack
nodes.source_location: image y=3.3 + '<!-- HOTEL & RESIDENCE -->' paths + '<!-- DOHA -->' paths
nodes.rationale: A three-tier mark, explicitly sectioned by comments in the file: the STEIGENBERGER raster wordmark on top; HOTEL & RESIDENCE beneath it as silver #C0C5C7 outlined glyphs at y approx 21-30; and DOHA below that, centred, in cream #EDEAE4 at y approx 41-48. The artwork is what settles the property's full name as 'Steigenberger Hotel & Residence Doha' — two lines, two sizes, two colours — a distinction that collapses whenever the mark is attempted as live text.

nodes.label: Specimen Name and Number
nodes.source_location: 26 paths at y approx 281-295: 19 fill=#EDEAE4 at x 26-191, 7 fill=#D6BE8A at x 461-514
nodes.rationale: The placeholder cardholder identity baked into the design export as outlined glyphs rather than live text: a cream #EDEAE4 name at the lower left and a muted-gold #D6BE8A member number at the lower right, sharing one baseline band. These are the only per-member values on the face, and being outlines they cannot be re-typed — which is precisely why the shipped asset deletes them. The four #EDEAE4 paths spelling DOHA sit in the same colour but were deliberately kept: that is lockup, not data.

nodes.label: card-back.svg (shipped card reverse)
nodes.rationale: The shipped reverse, loaded through by MembershipCardBack.tsx. Byte-for-byte identical to the design export (same 1,191,979 bytes, same MD5 70fdf21547332af8be8352a817e10f3a) — the supplied artwork used unchanged, in contrast to the face, which needed two edits. Because an SVG loaded through cannot receive per-member React content, the live QR symbol is laid over the artwork's own white well rather than drawn into the file.

nodes.label: card-face.svg (shipped card front)
nodes.rationale: The shipped front of the membership card, served as a static asset and loaded through by MembershipCard.tsx. It is the design export itself, not a CSS reconstruction: identical viewBox, identical Figma export symbol ids (clip0_42_1891, mask1_42_1891, mask2_42_1891, paint0_linear_42_1891, image0_42_1891, image1_42_1891) and identical path geometry. Exactly two edits versus the source: the 26 outlined specimen glyph paths were deleted, and mask0_42_1891 with its two full-bleed white rectangles was deleted so the rounded corners stay transparent instead of showing white.

nodes.label: lockup.svg (Steigenberger brand lockup)
nodes.rationale: The brand lockup used over the hero on the auth screens: a hand-flattened 144x53 SVG, three orders of magnitude smaller than the card artwork (14 KB vs ~700 KB-1.2 MB). One embedded PNG for the STEIGENBERGER wordmark plus 19 outlined paths for the two property lines. Drawn at its natural size and never scaled, so its glyphs land within ~1px of where the 390px design board places them.

nodes.label: Privilege Guest Card Back (design export)
nodes.rationale: Design export of the reverse of the same card. A different toolchain than the face export (Inkscape/Scour-style output: 980 clipPaths, 2165 groups, 1475 paths, rgb-percentage stops, zoomAndPan/preserveAspectRatio attrs) and a different internal unit scale (404.88 x 255 user units mapped onto the same 540 x 340 rendered box by a 0.749 gradientTransform), but the same rounded-rect card silhouette and the same 48-stop charcoal ramp as the face. Contains a baked rounded white QR well; no embedded raster images.

nodes.label: Frame 1.svg (lockup design export)
nodes.rationale: The upstream design export the shipped lockup is derived from, named explicitly in lockup.svg's own header comment. It draws STEIGENBERGER as two overlaid 486x242 PNGs (artwork plus a separate luminance mask), which is why it could not be dropped in unmodified. Lives alongside the card exports in the svg files/ directory.

nodes.label: Privilege Guest Card Face (design export)
nodes.rationale: Figma export of the front of the Privilege Guest membership card, 540x340 with a 24-unit rounded corner. Vector-only (zero <text> elements: 1415 outlined paths, 964 luminance masks, 965 groups) over a 48-stop charcoal linear gradient, plus two 486x242 base64 PNGs (image0_42_1891 artwork + image1_42_1891 luminance mask) carrying the licensed STEIGENBERGER wordmark. Palette: 183 gold #B4954F paths (facade line art and 'PRIVILEGE GUEST' lettering laid into the building), 20 highlight #EBD79B, 15 silver #C0C5C7, cream #EDEAE4, muted gold #D6BE8A. This is the design source of record, still carrying specimen personalisation and a full-bleed white backing rectangle.

nodes.label: Ship the Export, Overlay the Live Text
nodes.source_location: diff vs design export: 26 glyph paths + mask0_42_1891 removed
nodes.rationale: The design file is shipped as the artwork and only the two fields that differ per member are re-added as live HTML text, positioned in the artwork's own 540x340 coordinate space at the coordinates the removed glyphs occupied (1cqw = 5.4 units, so registration holds at any rendered size). The alternative — rebuilding the face in CSS — could never work, because the wordmark is a licensed narrow serif that ships no webfont, so live text fell through to a stand-in stack and lost the HOTEL & RESIDENCE line, and the line art had to be hand-scaled into a box that never quite matched. Both edits are recorded so a re-export can be repeated. The white full-bleed rectangle had to go too: the export hides it under the gradient, but it showed at the rounded corners.
nodes.norm_label: ship the export, overlay the live text

nodes.label: Flattened Wordmark Composite
nodes.source_location: header comment + single <image x=2.6795 y=3.2995 width=137.6259 height=13.2027>
nodes.rationale: Stated verbatim in the file's own comment: the export draws STEIGENBERGER as two overlaid 486x242 PNGs — artwork plus a separate luminance mask — so any engine that does not composite the pair renders an opaque rectangle instead of a wordmark. The two are therefore composited once, ahead of time, into a single transparent image placed at the rect they shared, and the HOTEL & RESIDENCE and DOHA paths are carried over from the export unaltered. Rendered on top of each other, the export and the flattened asset are the same picture.

nodes.label: Outlet App HTML Entry
nodes.rationale: Vite shell titled 'Privilege Guest - Outlet'. A third front end that the System Overview's 'there is no third surface' claim predates.

nodes.label: Outlet Fulfilment Configuration
nodes.rationale: The guest announces, one outlet confirms. Throttle 60s, expiry 24h, sweep every 900s. OUTLET_NOTIFY_INCLUDE_NOTE is off unless the hotel has agreed the guest's free text may leave the system, because enabling it makes 'we never send names' false — a guest can type their own into that box.

nodes.label: Append-Only Audit Trail
nodes.rationale: Thirty-eight distinct actions including every member record viewed, every export, every authorisation denial and every refresh-token replay. Metadata carries membership numbers, never names; a failed sign-in against a non-existent account deliberately does not record the email tried, or the attacker's guesses would be written into the trail.

nodes.label: Eleven-Table Data Model
nodes.rationale: Member, ClaimCode, StaffUser, Benefit, BenefitRequest, Redemption, ConsentRecord, AuditLog, RefreshToken, OtpCode, MfaRecoveryCode. Constraints carry as much of the design as the application code. Money stored as integer minor units (fils), never floating point.

nodes.label: Staff Verification Page (02)
nodes.rationale: A web page, not a fourth product — opened on whatever device is already at the counter, so no installation or procurement. Staff sign in individually so every redemption is attributed to a named person. The system records; it does not discount.

nodes.label: Search-Engine Exclusion (noindex, nofollow)
nodes.rationale: Cites §9: a membership list is a record of named prominent individuals. Keeping the app out of search indexes costs nothing and removes one way its existence and structure become public.

nodes.label: Health Data Excluded by Construction
nodes.rationale: Spa treatment records can imply health information, so the redemption table has no column for a treatment or description and no endpoint accepts one — only that a spa benefit was used.

nodes.label: Two-Layer Log Redaction
nodes.rationale: The logger redacts known paths and a serialiser walks whatever it is handed removing anything named like personal data at any depth. Two mechanisms because either alone leaves a gap; the second is what makes an accidental 'log the whole member object' call safe.

nodes.label: Confidentiality of the Membership List
nodes.rationale: The membership list is the asset. The reference card is issued to a member of the Qatari ruling family; the list is a record of named prominent individuals and their movements. Treated as the primary design constraint rather than a later addition, which is why controls go beyond what a loyalty app would normally carry.

nodes.label: Single Administrator Account Type
nodes.rationale: Manager, support and outlet-staff roles from version 2 were removed. Only named Administrator accounts can sign in; legacy role values survive purely so historical records keep naming whoever acted, and are forced suspended by a database CHECK.

nodes.label: No Member List or Name Search for Staff
nodes.rationale: Staff can retrieve only the person in front of them, by exact number or scan. Given who these members are, that restriction is the point rather than a detail.
nodes.norm_label: no member list or name search for staff

nodes.label: Admin Dashboard Wireframes (03)
nodes.rationale: Members, member detail, reporting and benefit management — the 'backend access' the client described. Small by design: a list of dozens, not thousands, so a simple table beats an analytics product.

nodes.label: Per-Channel Consent, Unticked by Default
nodes.rationale: Qatar's data protection law requires explicit prior consent specifically for direct electronic marketing, so bundling it into activation would invalidate it. The printed sheet already promises notification by the member's preferred channel, making it a programme commitment rather than only a marketing preference.

nodes.label: Member App Screens (01)
nodes.rationale: Claim membership, verify consent, Explore, Offers, Benefit detail, Search, Digital card, Profile. Everything visible without tapping, because the paper sheet showed all five categories at once and hiding terms would be a downgrade.

nodes.label: Responsive Strategy
nodes.rationale: Member experience mobile-first widening at ~900px (tab bar becomes top nav, lists go one to three columns, list-and-detail split); admin desktop-first collapsing below it; verification page equal at both sizes. Desktop is not a wider phone and earns its place by reducing navigation, not expanding scope.

nodes.label: Arabic / Right-to-Left Planning
nodes.rationale: RTL affects sidebar position, table column order and text alignment on every screen, so it must be planned from the start rather than retrofitted.

nodes.label: Tap-to-Call Reservations
nodes.rationale: Described as the highest-value small addition in the build: three benefits require phoning three different numbers currently printed on a sheet that gets lost. Nearly free to implement and it removes genuine friction. On desktop the number is displayed rather than dialled.

nodes.label: Wireframes Draft 2 (docs copy)
nodes.rationale: Byte-identical duplicate of the root wireframes.html (74,932 bytes, diff clean). Two copies of the same artefact, not two documents.

nodes.label: Wireframes Draft 2 (revised scope)
nodes.rationale: Fourteen screens across three surfaces. Draft 1's points ledger, tiers, earn rates, segment/targeting engine, tenant isolation, POS integration and WhatsApp campaign layer were all removed after the client confirmed a single-property programme with a fixed schedule.

nodes.label: Pinch-Zoom Deliberately Allowed
nodes.rationale: user-scalable=no is deliberately absent: this runs on a shared counter device anybody on shift picks up, and pinch-zoom is how somebody reads a membership number they cannot quite make out.

nodes.label: No Points, Tiers or Balances
nodes.rationale: Version 1 assumed a multi-brand coalition with a points currency; the client narrowed scope twice. Nothing is earned, benefits are granted on joining, and one membership level means every member sees the same schedule. The schema comment states that a balance column appearing would be a misreading of the specification.

nodes.label: Masked Contact Details and Visible Access Notice
nodes.rationale: Phone and email are masked by default so revealing one is a deliberate, logged action. Telling staff on the screen itself that their viewing is logged is a stronger control than the log alone.

nodes.label: Stage 17 — Design System and Styling
nodes.rationale: Lower-risk than it sounds because the wireframe annotations were followed literally: this is styling a known thing, not designing an unknown one. The three apps share tokens and primitives but not layout. Accessibility already present (real buttons, associated labels, role=alert, aria-current) must not regress.

nodes.label: Stage 22 — Arabic and RTL
nodes.rationale: The item most likely to be underestimated. The UI half is cheap because Stage 17 used logical properties throughout, but benefit content lives in single-language database columns and needs a translation table. Also decide Arabic-Indic vs Western numerals, Gregorian vs Hijri dates, and which language message templates use.

nodes.label: Stage 23 — App Stores, Install, Push and Wallet
nodes.rationale: Play accepts a Trusted Web Activity wrapping the existing PWA; Apple does not accept PWAs at all and guideline 4.2 rejects repackaged websites. Install without a store is already built with vite-plugin-pwa. The identity payload is NetworkOnly because a cached credential fails at a spa reception with no useful error; benefits and profile are NetworkFirst so R14 still holds.
nodes.norm_label: stage 23 — app stores, install, push and wallet

nodes.label: Capacitor over React Native
nodes.rationale: Apple guideline 4.2 rejects repackaged websites, so a PWA wrapper alone fails review. Capacitor wraps the existing React member app and adds push, biometrics, Wallet and camera — one codebase, and the member app keeps working as a website. React Native is months plus a second codebase.

nodes.label: Wallet Pass Update Web Service Cost
nodes.rationale: The pass certificate is $0 inside the $99 membership, but a rotating QR means implementing Apple's pass update web service over APNs. Issuing a longer-lived credential instead is cheaper and weakens exactly the property the product says matters most.
nodes.norm_label: wallet pass update web service cost

nodes.label: Design Tokens in packages/ui, Not Tailwind
nodes.rationale: CSS custom properties consumed by all clients, each app overriding only semantic colour tokens. Chosen over Tailwind mainly for Stage 22: with CSS logical properties throughout, Arabic RTL costs one dir attribute rather than a per-class audit across three apps. Build-plan rule 1 (no styling) was retired deliberately, and no-styling.test.ts was renamed rather than deleted so its two load-bearing assertions survived.
nodes.norm_label: design tokens in packages/ui, not tailwind

nodes.label: BenefitTranslation Table for Arabic Content
nodes.rationale: Adding titleAr/termsAr columns is simpler but bakes 'two languages, forever' into the schema. A table keyed by benefit and locale makes a third language a row rather than a migration. Either way R14 still applies: an administrator changing Arabic terms must not need a deployment.

nodes.label: IDENTITY_CODE_HMAC_SECRET
nodes.rationale: Keys the code printed on the back of every physical card. Rotating it invalidates every card at once — which is also the only recovery a printed credential has, so it must be backed up before a print run.

nodes.label: SMTP Passcode Delivery
nodes.rationale: OTP_DELIVERY_CHANNEL defaults to smtp over Gmail on 465. Email is explicitly interim because no SMS provider was provisioned.

nodes.label: Invitation and Activation Flow
nodes.rationale: Onboarding runs backwards from a normal app: the hotel creates the account and the member claims it. 160-bit single-use code shown once and stored only as a hash; consumed inside the same transaction that activates the membership so two simultaneous attempts cannot both succeed. Reusable codes would let anyone holding a discarded letter join.

nodes.label: Member Guest App
nodes.rationale: Phone-first, public internet, seven screens: Activate, Sign in/Verify, Offers, Offer detail, Profile, Card.

nodes.label: Member OTP Sign-in
nodes.rationale: Phone number then a six-digit passcode valid five minutes, five attempts. No password ever exists for a member, so none can be reused from another breach.

nodes.label: Request, Decide, Record Loop
nodes.rationale: The flow the product exists for: a member never grants themselves anything. Pending, then approved or declined by a named administrator, then fulfilled by a separate redemption row. Enforced: one open request per benefit, one decision, one approval spent at most once (unique constraint), party-size caps checked at recording.

nodes.label: Account Enumeration and Timing Resistance
nodes.rationale: Passcode requests return the same response whether or not the number belongs to a member; a sign-in against a non-existent account still runs a full Argon2 verification against a dummy hash; unknown, expired, used and wrong-phone invitation codes all return one identical message.

nodes.label: Digital Card Without QR Credential
nodes.rationale: Earlier drafts specified a scannable rotating credential plus a counter-staff verification page. Version 3 removed both: a 40% spa discount is worth stealing, so a self-declared or screenshot-forwardable credential would be worth forging. Entitlement is established by a named administrator deciding a request, never by software trusting a presented code.

nodes.label: Rate Snapshot on Redemption
nodes.rationale: The discount percentage in force is copied onto the redemption row and never read back from the benefit. Changing dining from 25% to 20% changes tomorrow's offer without rewriting last month's record or restating a report already sent.

nodes.label: Rotating Digital Card Code
nodes.rationale: Draft 2 specified an opaque, automatically refreshing payload: these are high-value benefits, so a static code that could be screenshotted and forwarded would be worth real money, and a stale payload fails verification. The code identifies but does not authorise. Superseded in Version 3.

nodes.label: Member App HTML Entry
nodes.rationale: Vite shell titled 'Privilege Guest', carrying the full mobile web-app metadata set.

nodes.label: Member PWA and Status-Bar Metadata
nodes.rationale: viewport-fit=cover lets the fixed tab bar sit under the home indicator and use env(safe-area-inset-bottom), which layout.css accounts for. theme-color #221c1b matches theme.css and the manifest — a mismatch flashes on every launch. iOS ignores the manifest and reads apple-touch-icon and apple-mobile-web-app-* instead; black-translucent keeps the canvas running under the status bar rather than leaving a white band.

nodes.label: Fixed Benefit Discount Schedule
nodes.rationale: Five categories (F&B 25%, Rooms 30%, Spa 40%, Meetings 25%, Lifestyle 30%) with party-size caps. A fixed discount schedule, deliberately not a points currency.

nodes.label: Benefit Versioning and Attribution
nodes.rationale: The programme materials state benefits may change without notice, which made editability the most important configuration requirement: every value a member sees is a database row, never a constant. Each edit increments a version and records who made it.

nodes.label: Privilege Guest Program
nodes.rationale: An existing invitation-only hotel benefits programme at Steigenberger Doha run on printed letters and plastic cards; digitised because the member loses the paper sheet and the hotel has no data at all about usage.

nodes.label: Fairplex Narrow Font Drop-In
nodes.rationale: Licensed webfonts are not committed. The @font-face in src/theme.css already points at both FairplexNarrowOT-Book.woff2 and .otf, so the wordmark picks up a purchased file on the next reload with no code change.

nodes.label: Hero Image Drop-In Convention
nodes.rationale: The name after 'benefit-' is the offer's key shown in the admin dashboard next to the version number, so a new offer created there picks up a hero by someone saving benefit-<key>.jpg — only a non-.jpg extension needs a line in src/screens/heroes.ts. Missing files fall back to a dashed IMAGE placeholder, so a partial set is fine and a typo never shows a broken image. AVIF is unsupported before iOS 16.4. benefit-lifestyle.jpg is still outstanding.

nodes.label: Benefit Management as the Test of Delivery
nodes.rationale: Changing the F&B discount from 25% to 20% must be a form field. If it needs a developer and a release, the client does not have backend access regardless of how good the rest looks. Discounts, caps, phone numbers and terms are all configuration read at runtime.
nodes.norm_label: benefit management as the test of delivery

nodes.label: Counter Lookup Rate Limit
nodes.rationale: A membership number is sequential and printed on the card, so resolving one is metered (60 per account per hour) no matter who holds the credential. VERIFICATION_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS is 600.

nodes.label: Google Sheets Sync Configuration
nodes.rationale: Disabled by default; empty values accepted only while disabled, with startup validation requiring all credentials when true. PostgreSQL remains authoritative and Google failures never fail writes.

nodes.label: Google Sheets Mirror
nodes.rationale: Optional, one-way, off by default hotel-facing export. Carries membership numbers, usage counts and benefit configuration; deliberately excludes names, phones, emails, request notes, consents and audit records. A standing bulk disclosure that should be an explicit client decision.

nodes.label: Finding: 25 Failing Tests, One Cause
nodes.rationale: 344 of 369 tests pass. All 25 failures trace to one guard refusing member creation without an email while passcodes are delivered by email; two older test files create members without one and cascade. No product code is wrong, but a red suite hides the next real regression.

nodes.label: Pre-Launch Blockers
nodes.rationale: Green the suite and remove the stale secret; settle passcode delivery (SMS unprovisioned, email interim); hosting region and a Qatari data protection impact assessment (fine up to QAR 1,000,000 on its own); alerting; key management and rotation; an anonymisation endpoint; approve or drop the Sheets mirror.

nodes.label: Finding: SECURITY-REVIEW.md Documentation Drift
nodes.rationale: Lists secure cookies as deferred though implemented, states no security headers are configured though the edge sets a full policy, and refers throughout to three client applications and a verification page that no longer exist.

nodes.label: Finding: Stale VERIFICATION_SESSION_HMAC_SECRET
nodes.rationale: Reported as blocking a production start: docker-compose.prod.yml was said to still require a secret belonging to the removed verification page. The file as it now stands sets VERIFICATION_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS instead and contains no such mandatory secret, so this finding appears already resolved.

nodes.label: Mandatory Secret Interpolation (:?)
nodes.rationale: Every production secret uses ${VAR:?message} with no default, so a missing one stops the whole stack rather than silently using a known password. A committed default is a password in git history.

nodes.label: Argon2id Password Storage
nodes.rationale: m=65536, t=3, p=2, 16-byte unique random salt, 32-byte output; bcrypt at work factor 12 only if no maintained Argon2 binding exists. Algorithm and parameters stored alongside the hash so parameters can be raised and hashes upgraded transparently on next login. Constant-time comparison; minimum length rather than composition rules, screened against a breached-password list.

nodes.label: Password Pepper in a Key Management Service
nodes.rationale: Held in the KMS, not the database, so a stolen dump alone is not crackable. That non-colocation is the property the pepper exists for, and is the reason an environment variable is the nearest available substitute where no KMS exists.
nodes.norm_label: password pepper in a key management service

nodes.label: Staff Management Was Never Built
nodes.rationale: The build plan lists staff management in Stage 12; it did not exist. Three consequences: instant revocation from the dashboard could not be performed, breached-password screening could not be implemented because nothing set a password, and there was no MFA reset. Recorded rather than quietly widening scope, and suggested as Stage 25.

nodes.label: Argon2id Parameters Pinned in Code
nodes.rationale: m=65536, t=3, p=2 taken from the security specification. Making them environment-tunable adds a way to silently weaken password hashing via misconfiguration and buys nothing, so they are deliberately absent from .env.example.

nodes.label: Breached-Password Screening via HIBP k-Anonymity
nodes.rationale: Five characters of the SHA-1 leave the process, several hundred suffixes come back, the comparison happens locally. Fails open on a network error and logs that it did, because an outage must not stop somebody changing a password — the passwords people most urgently want to change are the ones already compromised.

nodes.label: /admin/staff Management Endpoints
nodes.rationale: StaffUser.tokenVersion and status were the mechanism behind instant revocation, both worked, and no endpoint reached either — so offboarding was a manual UPDATE against production. Three refusals: you cannot suspend yourself, suspend the last active administrator, or reset your own second factor. Never-your-own is the enforceable half of two-person control without causing permanent lockout at a hotel with one administrator.

nodes.label: Split JWT Audiences (member vs staff)
nodes.rationale: JWT_ISSUER derived from DOMAIN; JWT_AUDIENCE_MEMBER=pgp-member and JWT_AUDIENCE_STAFF=pgp-staff separate the two surfaces at the audience check.

nodes.label: Caddy Edge Proxy
nodes.rationale: Automatic TLS, HSTS, CSP, serves both apps and proxies the API. Refuses /admin/* from outside the hotel network on the API path itself, not merely on the panel's hostname — the UI is not the control.

nodes.label: Fastify API
nodes.rationale: One Fastify 5 process on Node 20 serving both surfaces. Route-level config hooks make deny-by-default enforceable at startup; Zod rejects unknown fields rather than ignoring them.

nodes.label: Deny-by-Default Route Authorisation
nodes.rationale: Every route must declare its required permission; an undeclared route prevents the server from booting rather than failing at runtime with a 403. A wrapper you must remember to call is exactly the control that fails under deadline. Public endpoints must say 'public' explicitly, so the opt-out is greppable.

nodes.label: Query Scoping in the WHERE Clause
nodes.rationale: Records are filtered in the database WHERE clause, never fetched then checked — fetch-then-check leaks existence through timing and error shape even when the response is a 404. The scope combinator uses AND rather than an object spread, because a spread would let a member's own identifier overwrite the one asked about. Held by fetch-then-check.test.ts.
nodes.norm_label: query scoping in the where clause

nodes.label: Refresh Token Rotation with Reuse Detection
nodes.rationale: Refresh tokens are single-use and grouped into families; presenting a spent one revokes the whole family, because a legitimate client never replays one. Stored in an httpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to one endpoint; a test strips comments from every client source and asserts no localStorage, sessionStorage or document.cookie use.
nodes.norm_label: refresh token rotation with reuse detection

nodes.label: Two-Audience Token Separation
nodes.rationale: A member token is rejected by an administrator endpoint at the audience check before it is inspected. Algorithm pinned to a fixed allowlist so alg:none and confusion attacks fail before the signature is examined.

nodes.label: Admin App HTML Entry
nodes.rationale: Minimal Vite shell titled 'Privilege Guest - Admin'. No PWA metadata and no viewport-fit, consistent with a desktop-only surface.

nodes.label: Administrator Password + TOTP Sign-in
nodes.rationale: Argon2id password screened against Have I Been Pwned, then a short-lived challenge (not a session), then a TOTP code. First sign-in forces enrolment; ten recovery codes shown once. An emailed code would not be a second factor.

nodes.label: Administrator Panel
nodes.rationale: Desktop, hotel-network only, six sections: Members, Requests, Redemptions, Benefits, Reports, Administrators.

nodes.label: Reporting and CSV Export
nodes.rationale: Usage by month, benefit and outlet; dormant members and members issued a card who never activated. Export carries membership numbers rather than names, is a separate permission capped at five per administrator per day, and every attempt is recorded.

nodes.label: INTERNAL_CIDR Network Restriction
nodes.rationale: Space-separated hotel staff/VPN CIDRs allowed to reach both the admin and outlet surfaces and their APIs. Guest Wi-Fi is excluded: network location is defence in depth while authentication remains the primary control.

nodes.label: Small-Cohort Suppression
nodes.rationale: Any figure backed by fewer than five distinct members returns 'insufficient data'. The cohort size itself is withheld, since publishing '3 members' is the same disclosure stated outright.

nodes.label: Environment Deviations
nodes.rationale: Docker is not installed on the development machine, so docker-compose.yml is written but unverified and a temporary PostgreSQL 18.4 cluster on 127.0.0.1:5434 stands in with pgp_owner and pgp_app roles mirroring the compose setup. Compose publishes on 5433 because 5432 is taken.

nodes.label: Local Startup: Four Processes
nodes.rationale: npm run db start then npm run dev brings up the API on :3000 and three Vite servers on :5173 (member), :5175 (admin) and :5176 (outlet), sharing one database. Allow about 20 seconds — an earlier check at 15s reported the API down when it was still starting.

nodes.label: What Is Not Covered by Tests
nodes.rationale: Stated so nobody mistakes a green suite for completeness: secrets are environment variables rather than a KMS, rate limiting is in-memory and resets on restart, and Docker is unverified because it is not installed on the development machine.
nodes.norm_label: what is not covered by tests

nodes.label: Operations Runbook
nodes.rationale: How to run it, how to verify it works, and what every failure actually hit here means. Written for whoever picks this up next.
